evidence: Conditional but supported path: close established seat S, which archives it (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:18); open fresh tab/pane P and agent to undo the closure (DESIGN-NOTES.md:232). Session-start instructions may run /seat (DESIGN-NOTES.md:238; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:30), and unbound /load may propose creation as well as resurrection/rebind (DESIGN-NOTES.md:193). If that plan creates fresh seat N and binds P before the user requests undo, the dedicated CLI then must adopt its current P into restored S (DESIGN-NOTES.md:263-265,272-274; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:46). The stated plan does not say whether N is retired, retained, or transferred, nor how N's new native-session history and thread relationships follow the rebind; the listed open details cover multi-object adoption and dependency conflicts but do not resolve this case (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:49). Thus a permitted ordinary boot order leaves the promised concrete adoption/restoration plan underdetermined and can leave a second live identity or incorrectly scoped history. This is a material recovery-contract gap, not a claim that every boot creates N or that data loss has occurred.
